question: Why is keeping a patient's bed nice and wrinkle-free so important?

options.A: Preventing pressure sores and skin friction
options.B: Enhancing the visual appeal of the ward
options.C: Keeping the mattress cool in warm weather
options.D: Making it easier to transfer the patient

explanation: Smooth sheets are a lifesaver! They get rid of ridges and friction points that can irritate delicate skin and cause painful pressure sores over bony areas. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why is making a bed considered a proper clinical nursing skill rather than just regular cleaning?

options.A: It gives the nurse a chance to check skin integrity
options.B: Hospital policies strictly forbid ward assistants from doing it
options.C: It requires advanced surgical training to perform
options.D: It is the only way to sterilize hospital mattresses

explanation: You're not just tidying up! While working on the bed, you get a great chance to closely observe the patient and spot early signs of skin breakdown. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h1)

question: What's the main reason you should never shake dirty bed linen in the air?

options.A: It creates loud noises that disturb resting patients
options.B: It wrinkles the fabric beyond easy folding
options.C: It causes the fabric threads to tear and wear out
options.D: It spreads dust and microorganisms around the room

explanation: Never shake those sheets! Shaking them sends germs and dust flying into the air where they can settle on other surfaces or be breathed in by everyone. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h2)

question: A nurse gets a sore lower back after making a few beds on a busy ward. What ergonomic mistake did she likely make?

options.A: Using cotton sheets instead of synthetic materials
options.B: Allowing the clean linen to touch the floor
options.C: Failing to adjust the bed height to waist level
options.D: Making an occupied bed with a partner

explanation: Protect your back! Working on a bed that's too low forces you to bend over constantly, which quickly strains your lower back muscles. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is the special job of a draw sheet placed right across the middle of the bed?

options.A: To serve as the primary pillow cover
options.B: To keep the patient's feet warm at night
options.C: To help lift and reposition the patient easily
options.D: To decorate the hospital bed for visitors

explanation: Think of a draw sheet as your helper sling! It spans the middle of the bed so you can slide or lift patients smoothly without causing friction burns. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h3)

question: Why should you gather all your clean linen before you even start making the bed?

options.A: To comply with hospital fashion and color codes
options.B: To prevent the clean linen from absorbing room temperature
options.C: To ensure the laundry department records the exact inventory
options.D: To avoid leaving the patient unattended or walking back and forth

explanation: Having everything ready saves you steps and keeps the patient safe by ensuring you don't have to walk away and leave them unattended. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is the main difference between an open bed and a closed bed in the ward?

options.A: Open beds are made without pillows or blankets
options.B: Closed beds are only used for surgical patients
options.C: The top covers are fan-folded to welcome a patient
options.D: An open bed does not require a bottom sheet

explanation: An open bed has its top covers neatly folded back, inviting an incoming or returning patient to easily slip right in. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h4)

question: Why do nurses create a 'toe-pleat' when finishing the top covers of a hospital bed?

options.A: To allow extra air circulation for patients with fevers
options.B: To keep the blanket securely fastened to the mattress frame
options.C: To relieve pressure on the patient's toes and prevent foot drop
options.D: To make the bed look neater for morning doctor rounds

explanation: That little pleat gives the feet wiggle room! It takes away heavy downward pressure, keeping the patient comfortable and helping prevent foot drop. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h4)

question: When making an occupied bed, why does the nurse ask the patient to roll away from them first?

options.A: To make it easier to administer oral medications from behind
options.B: To clear half the mattress for removing old linen and applying new sheets
options.C: To prevent the patient from grabbing the clean equipment tray
options.D: To ensure the patient looks out the window during the procedure

explanation: Rolling the patient away exposes one half of the bed, allowing the nurse to work efficiently on that side before switching. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h5)

question: While making an occupied bed, what is a crucial safety step before walking around to the other side?

options.A: Remove the patient's pillow to improve neck alignment
options.B: Lock the wheels of the bed in the highest position
options.C: Raise the side rail on the side the patient is facing
options.D: Turn off all overhead fluorescent ward lights

explanation: Always put safety first! Raising that side rail ensures the patient won't accidentally roll out while you walk around to the opposite side. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h5)

question: Where is the best place to leave the call bell after you finish making the bed?

options.A: Within immediate reach of the patient
options.C: On top of the bedside medication cabinet
options.D: Hung securely on the foot of the bed frame

explanation: Always make sure the call bell is right where the patient can easily grab it so they can call for help whenever they need it. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h6)

question: Why should you always return the bed to its lowest position and lock the wheels when you're done?

options.A: To keep the mattress springs from wearing out quickly
options.B: To comply with fire safety evacuation regulations
options.C: To prevent accidental falls and keep the bed stable
options.D: To make it easier for housekeeping to sweep the floor

explanation: A low, locked bed protects your patient from nasty falls if they try to get up, and keeps the bed steady during transfers. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h6)
